raw_case_text:
A 71-year-old male patient with a past medical history of SLE and lupus nephritis, who had been on prednisolone for 20 years, was referred to our hospital by his general practitioner after presenting with right arm swelling and erythema of 5 days duration that did not improve despite oral amoxicillin/clavulinic acid. A review of system was unremarkable for headaches, confusion, cough, sputum, shortness of breath, and fever. He had not been exposed to any bird excrement.
On admission he was afebrile, his blood pressure was 122/88 mmHg, pulse rate was 82/min, and respiratory rate was 18/min and was saturating at 98% on room air. He was noted to have left basal crepitation and bipedal edema. Skin examination (Figure 1) showed diffuse right upper limb pitting edema and erythema, with multiple 1-2 cm hemorrhagic tender bullae scattered over the forearm.
On day 1 of admission, blood cultures were taken, investigations were done (Table 1), and intravenous (IV) cefazolin was started. On day 3, antibiotics were escalated to IV piperacillin-tazobactam because of the temperature of 37.7 C, persistent swelling, and erythema.
Blood culture yielded CN on day 6 of admission and amphotericin-B was commenced. Lumbar puncture was performed which isolated CN on cultures. Antifungal therapy was optimized to liposomal IV amphotericin-B (AmBisome based on 4-5 mg/kg) and oral flucytosine 1 g Q12H (based on 25 mg/kg).
After further investigations (Table 2), clinical impression was for DC involving blood, CNS, lung, and skin involvement. Modest improvement in the skin infection was noted after starting antifungal therapy (Figure 2). Biochemically, CRP also downtrended (Table 3).
Blood culture was sterilised after 8 days of starting antifungals, but CSF culture remained positive for CN at day 10 of treatment (Table 4).
Prednisolone 15 mg/day was lowered to 10 mg/day after discussion with rheumatologist. Further hospital course was complicated by acute on chronic thrombocytopenia secondary to flucytosine, which led to discontinuation of flucytosine after 19 days of administration. He also developed worsening of chronic kidney disease (CKD), fluid overload, haemorrhoidal bleeding, and worsening of anemia. AmBisome was discontinued after 22 days, and the patient was terminally discharged to home in keeping with his wishes. He demised 30 days after initial presentation.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 71-year-old male on chronic prednisolone for systemic lupus erythematosus and lupus nephritis presented with a 5-day history of right arm swelling and erythema refractory to oral amoxicillin-clavulanate.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Over the 5 days prior to referral, the patient developed progressive right upper extremity swelling, erythema, and painful hemorrhagic bullae that failed to improve with outpatient oral amoxicillin-clavulanic acid.
subjective.past_medical_history: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), lupus nephritis, and chronic kidney disease, treated with oral prednisolone for 20 years. Denied exposure to bird excrement.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for right arm swelling, erythema, and tender hemorrhagic bullae. Negative for headache, confusion, cough, sputum, shortness of breath, or fever on admission. Home medications: prednisolone 15 mg/day and recent amoxicillin-clavulanic acid.

objective.physical_examination: Admission vital signs: afebrile (later 37.7 C on day 3), blood pressure 122/88 mmHg, pulse 82 beats/min, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, room air SpO2 98%. Left basal lung crepitations, bipedal edema, and diffuse right upper limb pitting edema and erythema with multiple scattered 1-2 cm tender hemorrhagic bullae over the right forearm.
objective.routine_investigations: Elevated CRP (which downtrended on antifungal therapy), baseline chronic kidney disease and anemia/thrombocytopenia, and blood cultures drawn on admission day 1 yielding Cryptococcus neoformans on day 6.
objective.advanced_workup: Lumbar puncture CSF fungal culture isolated Cryptococcus neoformans (remaining culture-positive on day 10 of treatment despite blood culture sterilization at day 8), and systemic staging confirmed disseminated involvement of the blood, CNS, lungs, and skin.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis of disseminated Cryptococcus neoformans infection presenting as bullous hemorrhagic cellulitis of the right forearm with fungemia, cryptococcal meningitis, and pulmonary involvement in a patient on 20 years of prednisolone for SLE/lupus nephritis, confirmed by isolation of C. neoformans from blood and CSF cultures. After initial empiric cefazolin and piperacillin-tazobactam, he was treated with IV liposomal amphotericin B (AmBisome 4-5 mg/kg/day for 22 days) and oral flucytosine (1 g every 12 hours, stopped after 19 days due to worsening thrombocytopenia) while reducing prednisolone from 15 mg to 10 mg/day. Complicated by worsening CKD, fluid overload, hemorrhoidal bleeding, and anemia, he was terminally discharged home per his wishes and died 30 days after initial presentation.
